config.title: Build typed parser combinator basics

intro.title: Build typed parser combinator basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a basic typed parser combinator library in TypeScript. You will learn how to create small, reusable parsing functions that can be combined to handle more complex input structures. The core concept involves using TypeScript's type system to ensure your parsers are type-safe and predictable. You'll work with fundamental TypeScript constructs like functions, generics, and custom types. By the end, you'll have a simple yet powerful toolkit for parsing structured text with full type support.
intro.usecase: Parser combinators are foundational in real-world applications that process structured text, such as form validation libraries, configuration file readers, and domain-specific language interpreters. For example, when building a dashboard that imports CSV data, typed parser combinators ensure each column is correctly parsed into its expected type (numbers, dates, strings) before visualization. In UI development, they power safe, incremental parsing of user input in complex form builders or query editors, providing immediate type feedback. This pattern is also key in tools like code editors' syntax highlighters or API request/response validators, where structured text must be reliably decomposed and validated.

objectives: Implement a basic parser type that accepts input and returns typed results
Construct simple character parsers using TypeScript's type system
Apply parser combinators to combine multiple parsers into complex ones
Manipulate parser results to transform parsed data into structured types
Initialize a parser library with typed helper functions for common patterns
Integrate error handling into parsers to manage invalid input scenarios
Configure parser behavior using TypeScript generics for flexible type inference

steps.title: Create the map parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a map function that transforms successful parser results while preserving type safety. Create a function named map that takes a parser and a transformation function, and returns a new parser with the transformed result type.
steps.hint: The map function should accept a parser of type T and a function that transforms T to U, then return a new parser of type U that applies the transformation on success.
steps.expectedOutcome: A map function that transforms parser results with proper TypeScript generics.

steps.title: Implement the choice parser combinator
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'choice' that takes an array of parsers and returns a new parser that tries each parser in sequence until one succeeds, with proper TypeScript union types for the result.
steps.hint: The function should accept an array of parsers with potentially different result types, and return a parser whose result type is a union of all possible parser result types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'choice' function that combines multiple parsers with proper type union handling for the result type.
successCriteria: The 'choice' function is defined, accepts an array of parsers, returns a parser, and handles union types correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Build the sequence parser combinator
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'sequence' that takes an array of parsers as input and returns a new parser that runs them in order, returning typed tuple results.
steps.hint: The sequence combinator should process each parser sequentially, accumulating results into a tuple while tracking the remaining input.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sequence function that accepts an array of parsers and returns a parser producing typed tuple results.
successCriteria: The sequence function is defined, accepts an array of parsers, and returns a parser that processes them in order with proper type handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The sequence combinator isn't quite right. Remember it should take parsers as input and return a parser that runs them in order, accumulating results.

steps.title: Create the many parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a function named 'many' that takes a parser and returns a new parser that applies it zero or more times, collecting results into a typed array.
steps.hint: The 'many' combinator should repeatedly apply the given parser until it fails, accumulating successful values in an array. Remember to handle the case where zero matches is valid (empty array).
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'many' function that returns a Parser<T[]> and correctly accumulates zero or more matches.
successCriteria: The 'many' function is implemented with proper TypeScript types and returns a parser that produces arrays of the inner parser's type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match the requirements. Review how to create a parser combinator that applies another parser repeatedly.

steps.title: Add optional parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a combinator function named 'optional' that makes a parser optional, returning a result with proper optional type handling.
steps.hint: The optional combinator should accept a parser and return a new parser whose result type is T | undefined. If the inner parser succeeds, return its value; if it fails, return undefined without consuming input.
steps.expectedOutcome: The optional combinator function is defined with proper TypeScript type annotations, handling both success and failure cases while preserving the rest of the input.
successCriteria: The optional function is implemented, accepts a Parser<T>, returns a Parser<T | undefined>, and correctly handles parser success/failure without consuming input on failure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your optional combinator correctly returns undefined on failure without consuming input, and has the proper return type Parser<T | undefined>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The optional combinator implementation is missing or incorrect. Review the concept: it should wrap a parser to make it optional, returning the parsed value on success or undefined on failure without advancing the input.
